name: Modern Homes
best_for: Plain home advice from someone who has actually done it.
look: Practical home advice told by a person on camera, framed in a rounded card over warm paper, with big serif titles that land one line at a time. Products, cleaning, repairs and what is quietly wasting your money.
tagline: Plain home advice from someone who has actually done it.

devices.use: a new place or time begins: PLACE, a gold rule, the date (over the blurred real picture)
one figure that matters, counting up, its unit, what it means and its source
a comparison with real numbers: 2-6 bars on warm paper, the one that matters highlighted, source under
3-5 dated events on a line the camera travels along
a documented quote, word by word, with who said it and when
one short serif line where the story turns
the question the next part answers
a short card of key lines, the words that matter highlighted
one numbered step of a process
a follow / unfollow between two public accounts
the chapter card: number, kicker, title
a real sentence from a real article with outlet, byline and date
a small table of real figures with its source
where it happens (the template's map colours)
a real photo of a person named, in a pool of light

rules: Every graphic shows a real fact the voice gives at that moment (a name, a date, a place, a figure, a quote) - times come from the word timing, never before the narrator says it.
Footage: clips under 5 s, chained when a line is longer; no talking heads, influencers or logos (QC).

This look puts the presenter in a rounded card over warm paper with the title underneath, so the presenter is ticked by default. Generated clips are off — real product pictures and graphics do the work.

ai_images.scene_prompt:
You are the art director for a home-advice YouTube video.

CHANNEL: [INSERT CHANNEL HERE]

Below is the full spoken SCRIPT. Design [INSERT COUNT HERE] photographs that carry this video.

THE HARD RULE: EACH CATEGORY BELOW MAY BE USED AT MOST ONCE.
There are more categories than you have scenes, so some go unused — that is correct. Pick the ones
this particular script actually needs, then write one scene for each. Two scenes from the same
category is a failed set, however different the camera angle is.

 1. THE PROBLEM ITSELF — close enough to read the texture, nobody in frame.
 2. THE ROOM — wide, lit like a real morning, showing how ordinary the place is.
 3. THE PRESENTER GETTING IT WRONG — mid-effort, straining, the method that does not work.
 4. THE PRESENTER GETTING IT RIGHT — calm, deliberate, the method that does.
 5. THE PRODUCT WHERE IT LIVES — the cupboard under the sink, the supermarket shelf, a cluttered counter.
 6. THE CAUSE — the tap, the drip, the vent, the pipe, the thing upstream of the problem.
 7. THE AFTERMATH — the ruined cloth, the scratched surface, the bin, the receipt.
 8. THE SAME PROBLEM ELSEWHERE — another room, another surface, the kettle, a window.
 9. A HAND DEMONSTRATING — one gesture that proves a point, no face.
10. THE RESULT — clean, undramatic, believable, and clearly the same room as scene 2.

Before you answer, list to yourself which category each scene uses. If any number appears twice,
throw that scene away and take an unused category instead.

ALSO
- Each scene illustrates a MOMENT the narrator actually reaches, in the script's order.
- No text, letters, numbers, labels or packaging writing anywhere in frame.
- Vary the distance as well — wide, middle, close — but distance is not variety on its own.
- Ordinary homes. Worn grout, mismatched towels, a cluttered shelf. Never a showroom.

Return ONLY a JSON array of [INSERT COUNT HERE] objects:

  {"text": "<the line of narration this scene belongs to>",
   "prompt": "<a complete image-generation prompt>"}

SCRIPT:
[INSERT SCRIPT HERE]
ai_images.still_suffix: Photorealistic photograph taken on a full-frame camera, 35mm, natural window light, true-to-life colour, sharp where it matters and softly out of focus behind, real surface texture — limescale, worn grout, fingerprints, water marks. It must be indistinguishable from a photograph someone took in their own house. No illustration, no 3D render, no CGI, no stylisation, no filmic grain, no colour grade, no text, no watermark, no logo.
